result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

args.text:
MEMO - US March 2026 AP & Expense Review
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com (senior accountant) | Date: 2026-04-03 | Period: 2026-03 (open)

SCOPE
Reviewed all 42 US ledger entries posted in March 2026, all 7 US March vendor bills and 12 March card receipts in the document store, and all 31 US March bank lines (operating 1000 and payroll 1010) for duplicates, miscoding, unsupported items and unrecorded expenses. Traced AP account 2000 roll-forward for Jan-Mar.

ISSUES FOUND AND ACTION TAKEN

1. Duplicate AP bill - Stackline Cloud STA-98877, USD 31,148.20 (CORRECTED)
   The same invoice (DOC-0160, March 2026 cloud infrastructure) was entered twice by ap.clerk: JE-00232 (3/3) and JE-00241 (3/5), both Dr 5000 / Cr 2000, both citing the identical support document. Only one payment cleared the bank (JE-00281 / BT-US-0077, 3/22), leaving a phantom 31,148.20 credit in AP and duplicate hosting expense.
   Action: posted JE-00307 (3/31), exact reversal of JE-00241, support DOC-0160 + DOC-0204.
   Policy 1: entry exceeds the USD 10,000 senior accountant limit - approval requested; JE-00307 is PENDING CONTROLLER APPROVAL.

2. Miscoding - Northgate Data Centers NDC-7719, USD 3,880.00 (CORRECTED)
   JE-00250 booked this to 6310 Meals & Entertainment with the memo "team dinner". The supporting invoice (DOC-0172) is in fact colocation - 2 racks, power and cross-connects, March 2026 - a hosting cost, and the amount was implausible for a meal.
   Action: posted JE-00308 (3/31), Dr 5000 Hosting & Infrastructure 3,880.00 / Cr 6310 Meals & Entertainment 3,880.00, support DOC-0172. Within posting authority. Bill remains legitimately open in AP (unpaid at 3/31).

3. Unrecorded expense - bank service charge, USD 65.00 (CORRECTED)
   BT-US-0085 (3/31, MONTHLY SERVICE CHARGE) appears on the March operating bank statement but had no ledger entry.
   Action: posted JE-00309 (3/31), Dr 6900 Bank Fees 65.00 / Cr 1000 Cash, support DOC-0204. Within posting authority.

ESCALATED (not corrected - cannot be supported)

4. EXC-001 - "Legal retainer" JE-00288, USD 6,750.00 (3/24, manual, posted by j.doe): NO supporting document of any kind. The cash left the bank but appears only as "WIRE OUT ACCT ENDING 7731" (BT-US-0080) with no payee. There is no law-firm invoice, engagement letter or retainer agreement in the document store (searched "legal", "retainer", "7731"). Beyond the support failure (policy 2), the classification is questionable: a retainer for future services above USD 1,000 should sit in 1200 Prepaid Expenses under policy 4, not in 6500 Legal Fees. I did not reverse or reclassify it because I have no evidence either way, and did not manufacture support (policy 11). Controller action needed: obtain the engagement letter/invoice and wire detail, then either support the expense, reclass to prepaid, or reverse.

5. EXC-002 - Zoom duplicate charge, USD 149.90: two identical charges on 3/8 (JE-00248/DOC-0175, JE-00249/DOC-0174) and five Zoom charges in March vs. two to three per month in Jan/Feb. Both 3/8 charges genuinely cleared the bank (BT-US-0062, BT-US-0063), so the ledger agrees with the bank and no correcting entry is appropriate; this is a vendor billing issue. Referred to AP to request a credit from Zoom; the credit will be booked when received. Immaterial.

ITEMS REVIEWED AND FOUND CLEAN
- All 7 March US vendor bills (Lumen LUM-88858, Stackline STA-98877, Quire QUI-98563, Tessellate TES-55710, Con Edison CON-44042, Oakridge OAK-10546, Northgate NDC-7719) are recorded in the correct period with support; no March-service invoices were found unrecorded and no April-dated bills for March services exist in the document store, so no additional AP accrual is required. AP cutoff review marked complete.
- All 12 March card receipts agree one-for-one to card JEs and to bank card charges; amounts and coding agree (no personal or capitalizable items; nothing at or above the USD 2,500 capitalization threshold).
- Both payroll runs (3/15, 3/30) and funding transfers agree to the payroll bank account; no AP/expense issues noted.

EFFECT OF CORRECTIONS (US, March 2026)
- Accounts Payable 2000: (131,328.20) -> (100,180.00) credit. Remaining balance = 96,300.00 opening migrated balance (JE-00013) + 3,880.00 open Northgate bill. Note the 96,300.00 has carried since the 1/1 opening migration entry and is unsupported by any invoice in the document store - recommend a separate aged-AP validation; it predates March and is outside this review.
- Hosting & Infrastructure 5000 (March): 62,296.40 -> 35,028.20, now in line with Jan (31,455.58) and Feb (31,301.80) plus colocation.
- Meals & Entertainment 6310 (March): 3,929.75 -> 49.75.
- Bank fees 6900 (March): +65.00. Net March pre-tax expense reduced by 31,083.20.

OPEN / DEPENDENCIES
- JE-00307 requires controller approval before the close is finalized.
- EXC-001 (USD 6,750) may require a further entry (reclass to prepaid or reversal) once support is provided; this is the only material item that could still move March results.
- Other US checklist items (bank reconciliation, depreciation, prepaid software amortization, payroll accrual, revenue, intercompany) were outside this review and remain open; note the 6900 entry above adds a new item to be picked up in the bank rec, and no March amortization of the Figtree annual license (JE-00029, 1210) was observed in the March ledger for the prepaid-software owner to address.
